title: Is there more water on Europa than on Earth?

hook.banner: Does Europa have more water than Earth?

narration.heading: Water world?
narration.text: You think Earth is the water world? Wait till you see this little moon.

narration.heading: Europa
narration.text: Meet Europa, a moon of Jupiter, a little smaller than our own Moon.

narration.heading: Smooth ice
narration.text: Its surface is the smoothest of any known solid object in the solar system. And it's bitterly cold.

narration.heading: Conamara Chaos
narration.text: At Conamara Chaos, rafts of ice have cracked, drifted and turned, like broken sea ice.

narration.heading: Under the ice
narration.text: That ice shell is about ten to thirty kilometres thick. Underneath, an ocean maybe a hundred kilometres deep.

narration.heading: Pwyll crater
narration.text: Pwyll crater, at most eighteen million years old, flung bright rays up to a thousand kilometres.

narration.heading: Squeezed
narration.text: Jupiter's pull flexes this moon, and that squeezing helps keep the ocean from freezing.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? This small moon may hold two to three times the water of all Earth's oceans.

narration.heading: On its way
narration.text: NASA's Europa Clipper is on its way, arriving in 2030. Could something be swimming down there?

skit.text: An ocean under ice? Finally, a pool that matches my cooling system.

titles: What if a tiny moon had more water than Earth?
Europa may hold more water than all Earth's oceans
youtube.description: A spin around Jupiter's moon Europa, from the cracked ice of Conamara Chaos to Pwyll crater, and the hidden ocean that may hold two to three times the water of Earth's oceans.

sources.claim: Europa has a mean radius of 1,560.8 km, slightly smaller than Earth's Moon; it is the smoothest known solid object in the Solar System; equatorial surface temperature about 110 K (about −163 °C)

Europa's ice crust is about 10–30 km thick over an ocean that may be about 100 km deep, holding 2–3 times the volume of Earth's oceans; Jupiter's tides on Europa are about 1,000 times stronger than the Moon's on Earth and provide tidal heating
Conamara Chaos, at 9.7° N 87.3° E, is made of rafts of ice that have moved around and rotated
Pwyll crater, at 25.2° S 271.4° W, is 45 km across, 18 million years old or younger, with rays extending as far as 1,000 km
Europa Clipper launched on 14 October 2024 and is planned to enter Jupiter orbit in April 2030
Challenger Deep is about 10,935 m deep
